subject: physics
title: Rutherford Range
summary: Fire an alpha particle at a nucleus to a marked distance, then name the element from where it turns back.
ncertRef: Section 12.2, Alpha-particle scattering and Rutherford’s nuclear model of atom
concepts: Energy conservation in a repulsive field
Nuclear charge from the turning point
learningOutcome: The student can find the distance of closest approach d = 2Ze²/(4πε₀K) of an alpha particle, and use it to find the energy needed or the charge of the nucleus.

levels.title: Alpha’s closest approach
levels.adds: Baseline: at the turning point K = (2e)(Ze)/(4πε₀d), so d = 2Ze²/(4πε₀K) (Example 12.2).
hints: All the kinetic energy has become electric potential energy at the closest point.
d = 2Z × 1.44 MeV fm / K, with K in MeV and d in fm.

levels.title: Sonar’s foil
levels.adds: New idea: with the energy fixed, d grows with Z, so a measured turning point gives the nuclear charge (Ex 12.2; Example 12.1).
hints: For one fixed energy, d is proportional to Z.
Round to the nearest whole number: Z is an integer.

misconceptions: The α-particle is stopped by hitting the surface of the nucleus
Heavier nuclei always turn the α-particle back closer to the nucleus
The positive charge of the atom is spread through its whole volume
